question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, Regulation 23, how frequently must Category I and Category II AIFs undertake valuation of their investments by an independent valuer, and under what condition can this period be extended?

answer.text: Once every 3 months by default; extendable to 6 months with 51% investor approval by value
Once every year by default; extendable to 2 years with 50% investor approval by number
Once every 6 months by default; extendable to 1 year with 75% investor approval by value of investment
Once every 6 months by default; extendable to 1 year with unanimous investor approval

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.13 and Regulation 23(2): Cat I/II AIFs must value investments at least once every six months by an independent valuer. This period can be extended to one year with approval of at least 75% of investors BY VALUE of their investment in the AIF. The Trap: 3 months is Cat III open-ended NAV frequency (different rule). Unanimous is too strict. 'Number' vs 'value' threshold is a common trap — SEBI uses value-weighted. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) asks the same fact; XIX-C demands you cite Regulation 23 and understand the 75%-by-value mechanics for the LPAC resolution. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always build the 1-year extension option into your PPM upfront. Going back to LPs mid-fund to change valuation frequency can spook investors — pre-authorise it in the Contribution Agreement.
